title: Reconciliation: Matching Your Ledger Against Theirs

questions.question: A double-entry ledger has a clean trial balance every day. Which of these errors can it still contain?
options: An entry whose debits exceed its credits by one cent
A settlement webhook that was posted twice with two different entry ids
A posting whose currency differs from the others in its entry
A journal entry that was edited in place after posting
questions.explanation: Both copies of the doubled webhook are balanced entries, so the trial balance cannot see them; only comparison against the processor's statement reveals that one event became two postings. The other three options are rejected by the ledger itself (balance rule, per-currency netting, append-only journal).

questions.question: Our ledger has reference ch_1007 once; the processor statement has it three times with the same amount. What does pass 1 produce?
options: Three EXACT_REFERENCE matches, since the amounts agree
One match and two MISSING_OURS breaks for the extra lines
One EXACT_REFERENCE match and two DUPLICATE_THEIRS breaks
One AMOUNT_MISMATCH break because the totals per reference differ
questions.explanation: Pass 1 pairs min(1, 3) = 1 copy and labels the excess on the longer side as duplicates of that side. MISSING_OURS is reserved for references our side has never seen at all; a reference we do have, with extra copies on their side, is a duplicate, which points the analyst at the counterparty's file rather than at a lost webhook.

questions.question: Why is the amount comparison in pass 2 exact while the date comparison has a tolerance?
options: Because dates are strings and cannot be compared exactly across formats
Because settlement dates legitimately drift across cut-offs, while a cent difference is a real finding
Because the Money type has no tolerance operation and dates do
Because amounts are already rounded by the processor before the file is sent
questions.explanation: Time zones and cut-off times move a settlement by a day without anything being wrong. A one-cent amount difference, by contrast, means the two systems disagree about the money, and absorbing it as a match hides exactly the rounding bugs that reconciliation exists to find. Money certainly could compare with a tolerance; the design chooses not to.

questions.question: The report shows ledger total 2145.42, statement total 2103.64, ours unmatched 100.88, theirs unmatched 59.10. Does it tie out?
options: No, because 2145.42 - 2103.64 is not equal to 100.88 + 59.10
Only if the matched total is exactly half of the ledger total
It cannot be determined without the count of matches
questions.explanation: The tie-out identity is ledger total minus statement total equals ours unmatched minus theirs unmatched (a difference, not a sum). 41.78 on both sides means every record is in exactly one match or break. The matched total is implied (2044.54) and does not need to be a particular fraction of anything.

questions.question: Why does the matcher group references in a TreeMap and sort both inputs before any decision, instead of using a HashMap on the input as received?
options: Because TreeMap lookups are measurably faster than HashMap lookups for string keys
Because HashMap cannot hold ArrayList values without an extra layer of boxing
So that the fuzzy pass can run a binary search over the sorted reference strings
So that two runs on the same data produce byte-identical reports usable as evidence
questions.explanation: HashMap iteration order is unspecified and input files arrive in arbitrary order, so without sorting, tie-breaks in pass 2 and the order of breaks could differ between runs. A report that changes between identical runs is useless to a controller or auditor. TreeMap is slower, not faster, than HashMap; the trade is made for determinism.

questions.question: A MISSING_THEIRS break appears on the last day of the period for a capture made that afternoon. What is the right action?
options: Carry it forward as a timing difference and expect it to match on tomorrow's statement
Post an adjusting entry reversing the capture so the books agree with the statement
Edit the original posting's date to the next period so it drops out of this run
Reclassify it as MISSING_OURS since the processor is the source of truth
questions.explanation: A capture that has not yet settled is the most common reason for MISSING_THEIRS and is not an error. Reversing it would be wrong the moment the money arrives, and editing a posting violates the append-only journal. It stays open and ages; only if it never settles does a reversal become appropriate.
